bull_bear.body:
- Established engineering capabilities and a customer-centric delivery model, which management cites as the basis for winning OPD and product-engineering work
- Long-standing client relationships across North America, Europe, Australia and parts of Africa
- Matured and proven quality management systems certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 27001:2022, supporting a well-matured development process with departmental performance objectives reviewed monthly
- In-built, continuous R&D within the software development process, including development of reusable application engines, codes and libraries
- Debt-free balance sheet: the Debt Equity ratio is disclosed as 0% for both 31.03.2026 and 31.03.2025
- US on-shore presence through a wholly owned subsidiary in operation since 1997, giving a long-established front end in its primary market
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic revenue concentration in North America — Management explicitly flags its continued dependence on the North American market, which contributes approximately 85% of revenue (Rest of the World 15%). Any slowdown in US enterprise technology spending, or a change in US trade or immigration policy, transmits almost directly to the top line. The stated mitigation is selective diversification into Europe, Australia and Africa, which is aspirational rather than achieved.
- AI-driven disruption of the software services delivery model — The MD&A names rapid technology obsolescence, disruption to traditional software development and service delivery models, and pricing and margin pressures arising from AI-driven productivity as risks. For an effort-priced offshore services business, AI productivity gains can compress billable hours faster than volume replaces them, and the required response is continuous reinvestment in reskilling and new capabilities.
- Single-activity and single-segment concentration in offshore software services — Essentially all standalone revenue is offshore software services, and the Company states it has strategically increased that focus. There is no second business line to cushion a downturn in the OPD / product-engineering demand pool, and the Company discloses no order book or pipeline that would give visibility.
- Dependence on availability and retention of skilled technology professionals — Management flags challenges relating to the availability and retention of skilled professionals in emerging technology domains. Talent is the productive asset of the business; recruiting and retaining good talent is described as one of the Company's top priorities, and wage and reskilling costs are the primary margin lever the Company does not control.
- Foreign exchange exposure on an export-only revenue base — Management flags foreign exchange fluctuations as a challenge. Revenue is earned in foreign currency while the cost base is largely rupee, so margins are rate-sensitive. The Company states it has a formal Board-approved hedging strategy reviewed periodically and that there is no commodity price risk.
- Cybersecurity and information-security obligations — The MD&A cites increasing cybersecurity and regulatory requirements as an industry condition, and the Company's response is to strengthen its information security and risk management framework. For a vendor handling client product code and data, a security failure is a client-loss and liability event as well as a compliance one; the Company relies on its ISO 27001:2022 certification here.
- Geopolitical, trade-policy and macroeconomic sensitivity of discretionary technology spend — Management states that ongoing geopolitical developments, changes in international trade policies and global economic uncertainties may influence enterprise technology spending and project execution timelines, and that the year saw measured enterprise spending particularly on discretionary technology spends. Project deferrals hit a services business as revenue timing risk, not just demand risk.
- Intense global competition in a commoditising service market — The MD&A describes an industry operating with intense global competition, evolving customer expectations and rapid technological change. As a small-cap offshore vendor CG-VAK competes against far larger Indian and global firms for the same OPD and modernisation budgets, which constrains pricing power. Separately, the Board states that at present the Company has not identified any element of risk which may threaten the existence of the Company, which is a notably unqualified assertion against the risk list the MD&A itself sets out.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: CG-VAK Software and Exports Limited provides offshore software services and Outsourced Product Development (OPD) to enterprise clients, with capabilities in product engineering, cloud and data analytics, application development and modernisation, and AI-enabled software engineering. The Company serves clients across North America, Europe, Australia and parts of Africa, and states its business is entirely software development rather than manufacturing. Delivery is run from offices in India with a wholly owned marketing and client-facing subsidiary in the USA, CG-VAK Software USA Inc.
business.title: What they do

business.body: - **Offshore Software Services:** Outsourced Product Development (OPD), Product Engineering, Cloud, Data Analytics, Enterprise application development and modernisation, AI-enabled software development and Agentic AI solutions
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Established engineering capabilities and a customer-centric delivery model, which management cites as the basis for winning OPD and product-engineering work
- Long-standing client relationships across North America, Europe, Australia and parts of Africa
- Matured and proven quality management systems certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 27001:2022, supporting a well-matured development process with departmental performance objectives reviewed monthly
- In-built, continuous R&D within the software development process, including development of reusable application engines, codes and libraries
- Debt-free balance sheet: the Debt Equity ratio is disclosed as 0% for both 31.03.2026 and 31.03.2025
- US on-shore presence through a wholly owned subsidiary in operation since 1997, giving a long-established front end in its primary market
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the Company's position as a preferred technology partner, with Outsourced Product Development (OPD) remaining a key pillar of the growth strategy focused on product development, modernization, cloud adoption and AI enablement
- Increase investments in Artificial Intelligence technologies, tools and platforms, including AI-enabled software development and Agentic AI solutions, alongside employee upskilling
- Strengthen capabilities in Outsourced Product Development (OPD), Product Engineering, Cloud and Data Analytics
- Strategically increase focus on offshore software services, which now accounts for substantially all of standalone revenue
- Make additional investments in sales and marketing, including strengthening the senior sales and business development leadership team, to accelerate customer acquisition and deepen existing customer relationships
- Keep North America as the primary focus market while selectively expanding into Europe, Australia, Africa and other strategic international markets to diversify the customer base and geographic mix
- Strengthen the information security and risk management framework and maintain prudent, Board-approved foreign exchange hedging practices
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company discloses no physical capacity or plant expansion programme; it is an asset-light offshore software services business and the Corporate Governance report states the Company does not have plants, only offices. Expansion is described entirely as capability and footprint build-out: increasing investments in Artificial Intelligence technologies, tools and platforms (including AI-enabled software development and Agentic AI solutions), strengthening capabilities in Outsourced Product Development, Product Engineering, Cloud and Data Analytics, and additional investments in sales and marketing including a strengthened senior sales and business development leadership team. Geographically, North America remains the primary focus market with selective expansion planned across Europe, Australia, Africa and other strategic international markets. R&D is described as in-built in the software development process, through development of application engines, reusable codes and libraries; no technology was imported in the last three years and none was absorbed from outside. No commissioning dates, project names or rupee capex quantum are stated for any of this. The Company has one wholly owned subsidiary, CG-VAK Software USA Inc., and states it has no other subsidiary, joint venture or associate; no acquisition or new-entity formation is disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Enterprise spending is expected to remain focused on AI-led transformation, cloud-native technologies, cybersecurity, data modernization and application modernization
- Adoption of AI, cloud computing, digital engineering, intelligent automation, data analytics and cybersecurity is expected to drive sustained demand for software product engineering, OPD, cloud modernization, enterprise application development and digital transformation services
- AI is increasingly moving from experimentation to enterprise-level deployment, creating opportunities across the technology value chain
- The Indian technology industry grew an estimated 6.1% in 2025 and is expected to surpass $315 billion in total revenues with technology exports exceeding $246 billion
- The global economy is expected to grow at around 3.0% during calendar year 2026, though geopolitical tensions, evolving trade policies and inflationary pressures may continue to influence technology spending
- Measured enterprise spending, particularly on discretionary technology spends, remains a headwind on near-term demand
- Demand for specialized talent and continuous upskilling is likely to remain important as technology and delivery models evolve
- AI-driven productivity is expected to create pricing and margin pressure on traditional software development and service delivery models

North America will remain the primary focus market while the Company selectively expands its presence across Europe, Australia, Africa and other strategic international markets.
OPD will continue to be a key pillar of the Company's growth strategy, with a focus on product development, modernization, cloud adoption and AI enablement.
The Company will increase investments in AI technologies, tools and platforms, including AI-enabled software development and Agentic AI solutions, with no rupee quantum or completion date stated.
The Company will invest further in sales and marketing and strengthen its senior sales and business development leadership team to accelerate customer acquisition.
The Company will selectively expand its presence across Europe, Australia, Africa and other strategic international markets, with no named location or date.

risks.note: The MD&A describes an industry operating with intense global competition, evolving customer expectations and rapid technological change. As a small-cap offshore vendor CG-VAK competes against far larger Indian and global firms for the same OPD and modernisation budgets, which constrains pricing power. Separately, the Board states that at present the Company has not identified any element of risk which may threaten the existence of the Company, which is a notably unqualified assertion against the risk list the MD&A itself sets out.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: CG-VAK Software and Exports is a Coimbatore-based offshore software services and Outsourced Product Development (OPD) exporter whose delivery is anchored in North America, which contributes approximately 85% of revenue.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: CG-VAK Software and Exports Limited provides offshore software services and Outsourced Product Development (OPD) to enterprise clients, with capabilities in product engineering, cloud and data analytics, application development and modernisation, and AI-enabled software engineering. The Company serves clients across North America, Europe, Australia and parts of Africa, and states its business is entirely software development rather than manufacturing. Delivery is run from offices in India with a wholly owned marketing and client-facing subsidiary in the USA, CG-VAK Software USA Inc.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- CG-VAK Software USA Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary in the USA, 100% holding, acquired 21.08.1997; reporting currency USD; provides marketing services to the parent and is the Company's front end in its primary North American market. The Company states it has no other subsidiary, joint venture or associate.
- CG Vak Software and Exports Limited Employees Gratuity Trust — related party: Gratuity trust; an income-tax approved irrevocable trust fund to which the Company contributes to finance plan liabilities, with assets invested in insurer managed funds.
- Mr. G. Suresh — related party: Key Managerial Personnel; Chairman & Managing Director; eligible for 1% commission on net profits which he has waived.
- Mrs. S. Latha — related party: Key Managerial Personnel; Non-Executive Women Director; the Company pays her rent and holds a rent deposit with her for premises used by the Company.
- Mr. C. Ganapathy — related party: Non-Executive Chairman (deceased 01.07.2025); received sitting fees until cessation.
- Mr. P. S. Subramanian — related party: Key Managerial Personnel; Chief Financial Officer.
- Mr. Harcharan J — related party: Key Managerial Personnel; Company Secretary & Compliance Officer.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Offshore Software Services:** Outsourced Product Development (OPD), Product Engineering, Cloud, Data Analytics, Enterprise application development and modernisation, AI-enabled software development and Agentic AI solutions

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- North America (approximately 85% of business)
- Rest of the World (15% of business)
- Europe
- Australia
- Parts of Africa

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Enterprise spending is expected to remain focused on AI-led transformation, cloud-native technologies, cybersecurity, data modernization and application modernization
- Adoption of AI, cloud computing, digital engineering, intelligent automation, data analytics and cybersecurity is expected to drive sustained demand for software product engineering, OPD, cloud modernization, enterprise application development and digital transformation services
- AI is increasingly moving from experimentation to enterprise-level deployment, creating opportunities across the technology value chain
- The Indian technology industry grew an estimated 6.1% in 2025 and is expected to surpass $315 billion in total revenues with technology exports exceeding $246 billion
- The global economy is expected to grow at around 3.0% during calendar year 2026, though geopolitical tensions, evolving trade policies and inflationary pressures may continue to influence technology spending
- Measured enterprise spending, particularly on discretionary technology spends, remains a headwind on near-term demand
- Demand for specialized talent and continuous upskilling is likely to remain important as technology and delivery models evolve
- AI-driven productivity is expected to create pricing and margin pressure on traditional software development and service delivery models

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strengthen the Company's position as a preferred technology partner, with Outsourced Product Development (OPD) remaining a key pillar of the growth strategy focused on product development, modernization, cloud adoption and AI enablement
- Increase investments in Artificial Intelligence technologies, tools and platforms, including AI-enabled software development and Agentic AI solutions, alongside employee upskilling
- Strengthen capabilities in Outsourced Product Development (OPD), Product Engineering, Cloud and Data Analytics
- Strategically increase focus on offshore software services, which now accounts for substantially all of standalone revenue
- Make additional investments in sales and marketing, including strengthening the senior sales and business development leadership team, to accelerate customer acquisition and deepen existing customer relationships
- Keep North America as the primary focus market while selectively expanding into Europe, Australia, Africa and other strategic international markets to diversify the customer base and geographic mix
- Strengthen the information security and risk management framework and maintain prudent, Board-approved foreign exchange hedging practices

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company discloses no physical capacity or plant expansion programme; it is an asset-light offshore software services business and the Corporate Governance report states the Company does not have plants, only offices. Expansion is described entirely as capability and footprint build-out: increasing investments in Artificial Intelligence technologies, tools and platforms (including AI-enabled software development and Agentic AI solutions), strengthening capabilities in Outsourced Product Development, Product Engineering, Cloud and Data Analytics, and additional investments in sales and marketing including a strengthened senior sales and business development leadership team. Geographically, North America remains the primary focus market with selective expansion planned across Europe, Australia, Africa and other strategic international markets. R&D is described as in-built in the software development process, through development of application engines, reusable codes and libraries; no technology was imported in the last three years and none was absorbed from outside. No commissioning dates, project names or rupee capex quantum are stated for any of this. The Company has one wholly owned subsidiary, CG-VAK Software USA Inc., and states it has no other subsidiary, joint venture or associate; no acquisition or new-entity formation is disclosed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established engineering capabilities and a customer-centric delivery model, which management cites as the basis for winning OPD and product-engineering work
- Long-standing client relationships across North America, Europe, Australia and parts of Africa
- Matured and proven quality management systems certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 27001:2022, supporting a well-matured development process with departmental performance objectives reviewed monthly
- In-built, continuous R&D within the software development process, including development of reusable application engines, codes and libraries
- Debt-free balance sheet: the Debt Equity ratio is disclosed as 0% for both 31.03.2026 and 31.03.2025
- US on-shore presence through a wholly owned subsidiary in operation since 1997, giving a long-established front end in its primary market

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geographic revenue concentration in North America — Management explicitly flags its continued dependence on the North American market, which contributes approximately 85% of revenue (Rest of the World 15%). Any slowdown in US enterprise technology spending, or a change in US trade or immigration policy, transmits almost directly to the top line. The stated mitigation is selective diversification into Europe, Australia and Africa, which is aspirational rather than achieved.
- AI-driven disruption of the software services delivery model — The MD&A names rapid technology obsolescence, disruption to traditional software development and service delivery models, and pricing and margin pressures arising from AI-driven productivity as risks. For an effort-priced offshore services business, AI productivity gains can compress billable hours faster than volume replaces them, and the required response is continuous reinvestment in reskilling and new capabilities.
- Single-activity and single-segment concentration in offshore software services — Essentially all standalone revenue is offshore software services, and the Company states it has strategically increased that focus. There is no second business line to cushion a downturn in the OPD / product-engineering demand pool, and the Company discloses no order book or pipeline that would give visibility.
- Dependence on availability and retention of skilled technology professionals — Management flags challenges relating to the availability and retention of skilled professionals in emerging technology domains. Talent is the productive asset of the business; recruiting and retaining good talent is described as one of the Company's top priorities, and wage and reskilling costs are the primary margin lever the Company does not control.
- Foreign exchange exposure on an export-only revenue base — Management flags foreign exchange fluctuations as a challenge. Revenue is earned in foreign currency while the cost base is largely rupee, so margins are rate-sensitive. The Company states it has a formal Board-approved hedging strategy reviewed periodically and that there is no commodity price risk.
- Cybersecurity and information-security obligations — The MD&A cites increasing cybersecurity and regulatory requirements as an industry condition, and the Company's response is to strengthen its information security and risk management framework. For a vendor handling client product code and data, a security failure is a client-loss and liability event as well as a compliance one; the Company relies on its ISO 27001:2022 certification here.
- Geopolitical, trade-policy and macroeconomic sensitivity of discretionary technology spend — Management states that ongoing geopolitical developments, changes in international trade policies and global economic uncertainties may influence enterprise technology spending and project execution timelines, and that the year saw measured enterprise spending particularly on discretionary technology spends. Project deferrals hit a services business as revenue timing risk, not just demand risk.
- Intense global competition in a commoditising service market — The MD&A describes an industry operating with intense global competition, evolving customer expectations and rapid technological change. As a small-cap offshore vendor CG-VAK competes against far larger Indian and global firms for the same OPD and modernisation budgets, which constrains pricing power. Separately, the Board states that at present the Company has not identified any element of risk which may threaten the existence of the Company, which is a notably unqualified assertion against the risk list the MD&A itself sets out.
